result.topic_en: Riemann examines the Wronskian-type expression $y'\,dy''/d\log x - y''\,dy'/d\log x$ for two branches of a P-function, determines its behaviour at the singular points $x=0,1,\infty$, and concludes that, multiplied by suitable powers of $x$ and $1-x$, it is a constant, so that it equals $C(1-x)^{\alpha'+\beta'+\alpha+\beta}x^{\alpha+\beta}$; he then introduces quotients $p$, $q$ of differences of branches.
